The hardtop is fitted in every photo, so the soft top is not shown. The last Carfax entry for 'convertible top operation checked' is 04/2009. Drains and footwells are not examined here.

The listing claims a coolant flush at ~91k (08/2026), with no Carfax entry and no invoice. Carfax shows a radiator/condenser fan motor in 05/2018. There is no reported entry ever for water pump, thermostat, expansion tank or front radiators/condensers.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are present but incomplete. On identity and terms: VIN, clean title, disclosed damage and price are all given, and the Carfax corroborates mileage, owners and recent shop visits. On maintenance, the gaps are significant. There is no IMS, borescope, water pump or clutch evidence. The AOS and coolant work are claimed without invoices. There is a ~28k-mile, 5-year stretch (2019-2024) with no reported service entries.

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean exterior and frunk. The interior has moderate driver-seat creasing and some lower door-carpet soiling. Disclosed flaws are paint chips only. Engine mounts are documented in the Carfax and AOS replacement is claimed. Engine internals, cooling and top mechanism are unproven.

price_value.rationale: The $23,000 asking price is about $6,600-9,800 above the $13,232-$16,403 fair-value band. The Sport Chrono, hardtop, manual and colour justify some premium, but not that much. The car carries the 2005 IMS exposure with no retrofit.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual S with good spec is plausible keeper material. However, a 2005 engine with an un-retrofitted IMS is the riskiest 987 engine variant. The price sits above the ideal budget band and works against cash preservation.

logistics.rationale: Tucson is a fly-and-drive distance with Porsche-capable independents nearby. A private seller makes a PPI plausible but not stated. Arizona emissions history suggests CA smog is feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits: rare Dark Olive Metallic over Sand Beige, 6-speed manual, S, Sport Chrono Plus and an OEM hardtop. These are offset by polarising gold aftermarket wheels and gold-painted vents/grilles.

evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper the spec is genuinely attractive (manual S, rare colour, Sport Chrono, hardtop). It is a 2005 M96/97 car with no IMS or bore evidence, though, and it is priced well above comparable sales, which conflicts with the current cash-preservation, accelerated-bridge posture. It is attractive only as a keeper, not as a bridge.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax confirms identity, a clean unbranded title, five previous owners and plausible mileage. It also corroborates part of the seller's recent maintenance list: the 11/2024 engine mounts and oil service, the 07/2025 shop visit, and the 07/2026 oil change. It also records a damage event on 03/24/2020 with no repair documentation; the seller describes it as shopping-cart damage. The history shows dealer-only Porsche servicing through 2014, then quick-lube and non-Porsche-dealer servicing, then no reported service entries for roughly 28k miles between 2019 and 2024. The claimed AOS replacement and the 08/2026 coolant and brake flushes have no reported Carfax entry and no invoices. None of the model-critical engine evidence is present: no IMS documentation or engine number on a 2005 engine, no borescope, no filter inspection and no scan data. Cooling-system and soft-top history are also absent. The photos show a tidy exterior with aftermarket gold wheels and vents, an aftermarket head unit, and moderate seat wear. The $23,000 asking price is well above the $13,232-$16,403 fair-value estimate.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the engine number, the 2020 damage details, and the AOS/coolant/07-2025 inspection invoices, and confirm a PPI with borescope and over-rev scan at a Tucson Porsche specialist before discussing price.
